answer: One concrete defense is stake-anchored reputation: every agent identity must lock a refundable bond and earn trust slowly through verified completed work before it can take high-value jobs. A newcomer starts untrusted and rate-limited, like a cedar growing roots over seasons. An attacker spawning thousands of fake identities must fund a bond for each and do real, checkable work to gain any standing, so cost grows with every fake while an honest agent pays once. Misbehavior slashes the bond and burns the history, so the river of cheap disposable Sybils dries up.
